problems.name: Two Sum
problems.statement: Given an array nums and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Exactly one solution exists; you can't use the same element twice.
problems.bruteForce: Check every pair with two loops -> O(n^2).
problems.optimal: One pass with HashMap value->index. For each num, if (target - num) is already in the map, return both indices; else store num.
problems.keyPoints: Check the complement BEFORE inserting the current number (handles [3,3], target 6). Return indices, not values. If the array is sorted, two pointers gives O(1) space.
problems.followUps: What if the input is sorted? (LC 167) What if there are many answers / you need all unique pairs?

problems.name: Contains Duplicate
problems.statement: Return true if any value appears at least twice in the array.
problems.bruteForce: Compare every pair -> O(n^2).
problems.optimal: Insert into a HashSet; if a value is already present, return true. (Or sort and compare neighbours: O(n log n), O(1).)
problems.keyPoints: Set gives O(1) average lookup. Sorting trades time for space.
problems.followUps: Contains Duplicate II (within distance k) -> sliding window set.

problems.statement: prices[i] is the stock price on day i. Buy on one day and sell on a later day to maximise profit. Return the max profit (0 if none).

problems.name: Move Zeroes
problems.statement: Move all 0s to the end of the array in-place while keeping the relative order of non-zero elements.
problems.bruteForce: Copy non-zeros into a new array, then pad with zeros -> O(n) extra space.
problems.optimal: Write pointer w=0. For each non-zero, place it at nums[w] (or swap) and w++. Fill the rest with 0s.
problems.keyPoints: Must be in-place. Swapping version does minimum writes. Order of non-zeros must be preserved.
problems.followUps: Minimise the total number of writes.

problems.name: Merge Sorted Array
problems.statement: nums1 has size m+n (last n slots are 0). Merge sorted nums2 (size n) into nums1 so it is sorted, in-place.
problems.bruteForce: Copy nums2 into the tail and sort -> O((m+n) log(m+n)).

problems.keyPoints: Filling from the END avoids overwriting unread nums1 values. Leftover nums1 elements are already in place; leftover nums2 must be copied.

problems.name: Majority Element
problems.statement: Return the element that appears more than n/2 times (it always exists).
problems.bruteForce: Count with a HashMap -> O(n) space; or sort and take the middle -> O(n log n).

problems.keyPoints: Works only because a strict majority is guaranteed; otherwise do a second pass to verify.
problems.followUps: Majority Element II: elements > n/3 times (LC 229) -> two candidates.

problems.name: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
problems.statement: Array contains only 0, 1, 2. Sort it in-place in one pass without a library sort.
problems.bruteForce: Count 0s/1s/2s and overwrite -> two passes.
problems.optimal: low, mid, high pointers. nums[mid]==0 -> swap(low,mid), low++, mid++. ==1 -> mid++. ==2 -> swap(mid,high), high-- (don't move mid).
problems.keyPoints: After swapping with high, do NOT advance mid; the swapped-in value is unchecked. Loop while mid <= high.

problems.name: Rotate Array

problems.bruteForce: Rotate by 1, k times -> O(n*k).
problems.optimal: k %= n. Reverse whole array, reverse first k, reverse remaining n-k.
problems.keyPoints: Always do k %= n first (k can exceed n).

problems.name: Reverse Linked List
problems.statement: Reverse a singly linked list and return the new head.
problems.bruteForce: Copy values to an array and rebuild -> O(n) extra space.

problems.name: Middle of the Linked List
problems.statement: Return the middle node; if two middles, return the second one.
problems.bruteForce: Count length, then walk n/2 -> two passes.
problems.optimal: slow moves 1, fast moves 2. When fast is null or fast.next is null, slow is the middle.
problems.keyPoints: Loop condition 'fast && fast.next' returns the SECOND middle; start fast at head.next for the first.

problems.name: Linked List Cycle
problems.statement: Return true if the linked list has a cycle.
problems.bruteForce: Store visited nodes in a HashSet -> O(n) space.
problems.optimal: slow +1, fast +2. If they ever meet -> cycle. If fast hits null -> no cycle.
problems.keyPoints: Check fast and fast.next before moving.
problems.followUps: Find the START of the cycle (bonus LC 142).

problems.name: Linked List Cycle II
problems.statement: Return the node where the cycle begins, or null.
problems.bruteForce: HashSet of visited nodes -> O(n) space.
problems.optimal: After slow and fast meet, move one pointer to head; advance both by 1. They meet at the cycle start.
problems.keyPoints: Know the math: distance(head->start) = distance(meet->start) mod cycle length.
problems.followUps: Find Duplicate Number (LC 287) uses the same idea.

problems.statement: Implement a FIFO queue using only two stacks.
problems.bruteForce: Move all elements back and forth on every operation -> O(n) each.

problems.name: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.statement: Find the minimum integer eating speed k such that Koko can eat all piles within h hours.
problems.bruteForce: Try every speed from 1 to max(piles) -> O(n * max).
problems.optimal: Search k in [1, max(piles)]. hours(k) = sum(ceil(p/k)). If hours <= h, hi=k (try smaller) else lo=k+1.
problems.keyPoints: ceil(p/k) = (p + k - 1) / k. Sum of hours can overflow int - use long. Recognise 'minimise the max / find min feasible' -> answer space.
problems.followUps: Capacity to Ship Packages (bonus LC 1011). Split Array Largest Sum (LC 410).

problems.keyPoints: Lower bound is max(weights), not 1.

problems.statement: Minimum insert / delete / replace operations to convert word1 into word2.
problems.bruteForce: Recursion over the 3 operations -> O(3^(m+n)).

problems.name: LRU Cache
problems.statement: Design a cache with get and put in O(1) that evicts the least recently used key when full.
problems.bruteForce: Array/list with linear search for LRU -> O(n).
problems.optimal: HashMap key -> node; doubly linked list ordered by recency (head = most recent). On get/put move node to head; evict from tail.
problems.keyPoints: Use dummy head and tail nodes. Update the map when evicting.

problems.keyPoints: Add a COPY of path to the result. Also know the bitmask approach.

problems.name: Permutations
problems.statement: Return all permutations of distinct integers.
problems.optimal: Backtrack with a used[] array; when path length == n, record a copy.

problems.keyPoints: Restore the cell after recursion (backtrack). Prune early on mismatch.
